speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned suffering from chronic diarrhea and lower abdominal discomfort; to begin my evaluation, how long have these symptoms been present, and have you noticed any blood or mucus in your stool?

speaker: Patient
text: 31-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing chronic diarrhea on most days for the past four months. She mentions lower abdominal discomfort and cramping, which is relieved by diarrhea. The patient notes the bowel movements are urgent, occasionally accompanied by mucus discharge, and often followed by a feeling of incomplete evacuation. She went camping several months ago and recalls another member of the camping party falling ill recently.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Inflammatory Bowel Disease (Ulcerative Colitis) or Infectious Colitis (Campylobacteriosis).

The patient's symptoms of chronic diarrhea, abdominal cramping relieved by defecation, urgency, mucus, and tenesmus (incomplete evacuation) are classic signs of colitis. The history of camping and a sick contact raises the possibility of an infectious etiology like *Campylobacter*, while the chronic duration (4 months) also suggests an inflammatory condition like Ulcerative Colitis.

REQUEST TEST: Fecal Calprotectin.
REQUEST TEST: Stool Culture and Ova and Parasite Exam.
REQUEST IMAGES: Colonoscopy.
